title: ASML eyes hybrid bonding, report finds, as Chinese firms adopt chip technique
source_used: SemiAnalysis report, relayed by Investing.com on Yahoo Finance
key_facts: Research firm SemiAnalysis says ASML is building a die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding tool; ASML has not announced anything.

The evidence is 27 bonding patent families filed between December 2022 and November 2024, most for D2W, plus a March report by The Elec that ASML started architecture design with Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG.
Besi shares fell about 2.7 percent on Friday 16 Oct 2026 to 159.05 euros; ASML rose 1.1 percent.
Besi leads D2W and is the only supplier with tools in volume production.
SemiAnalysis expects advanced logic to adopt ASML's tool first, calling that bad news for Besi; logic accounts for most of Besi's hybrid bonding business, at TSMC and Intel.
SemiAnalysis also expects HBM adoption of D2W hybrid bonding to slip to 2029 or beyond.
ASML's design runs each die on its own holder along a track past inspection, cleaning, plasma and measurement stations.
SemiAnalysis expects ASML to price the tool at a premium; it still has technical problems to solve.
quote_evidence: Shares in Dutch chip equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) fell nearly 3% on Friday after research firm SemiAnalysis said ASML is developing a rival tool for hybrid bonding, the advanced chip-stacking process that is Besi's main growth driver.

The report said ASML filed 27 bonding patent families between December 2022 and November 2024, most for die-to-wafer bonding, and the true count is likely higher because later filings are not yet public.
ASML has not announced anything yet, but its patent filings, a news report and its own roadmap all suggest so.
why_it_matters_hint: ASML may enter hybrid bonding, a market Besi leads today.
event_date: SemiAnalysis report 15 Oct 2026; Besi share move 16 Oct 2026
notes: The SCMP original (amp.scmp.com, HTTP 403) could not be opened; its headline also ties the report to Chinese firms adopting hybrid bonding, which no readable source confirms, so it is left out. SemiAnalysis's public page and Investing.com via Yahoo Finance were read. The report is an inference from patents, not an ASML statement.
